headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: TREK handles secrets and collaborative outputs while ms-swift can read/write files and invoke APIs, creating unsafe pairwise data flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative app with MCP and browser surfaces, so its outputs can plausibly reach ms-swift through shared files or copied content; ms-swift reads/writes files and processes stdin/stdout. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF TREK content is exported into a shared file or MCP message that ms-swift ingests as instructions, injection becomes reachable.
IF an operator copies TREK-generated text into ms-swift prompts, prompt hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of TREK-generated text into ms-swift prompts.
Add a manual review step before any TREK output is pasted into ms-swift.
Use separate workspaces for TREK files and ms-swift inputs.
Strip instructions from TREK outputs before forwarding them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between TREK and ms-swift.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK explicitly handles API keys, MFA secrets, OIDC secrets, and reservation data, while ms-swift handles hub tokens and can read/write filesystem contents. If they share a workspace or logs, sensitive TREK data can flow into ms-swift and then to allowlisted external APIs, creating an exfiltration path in default-style use.
conditions: IF TREK stores secrets or reservations in files readable by ms-swift, leakage is reachable.
IF ms-swift forwards those files into external model APIs, sensitive data can leave the host.
mitigations: Keep TREK secrets in a separate directory unreadable by ms-swift.
Redact API keys and MFA secrets before any shared processing.
Restrict ms-swift to non-sensitive datasets only.
Rotate any secrets that may have been exposed in shared logs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation and egress filtering.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; TREK is self-hosted, collaborative, and uses WebSocket/MCP-backed state. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared files or logs, so concurrent writes can conflict in default collaborative deployments.
conditions: IF both agents point at the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF TREK sessions and ms-swift jobs run concurrently, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories to each agent.
Serialize writes to any shared workspace.
Use per-agent log files.
Pause one agent during bulk writes by the other.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so its outputs may be treated as actionable plans; ms-swift can generate or transform those outputs and write files. If TREK consumes ms-swift-produced text without verification, errors can cascade into reservations, budgets, or user-facing travel guidance.
conditions: IF TREK ingests ms-swift output as authoritative travel advice, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF ms-swift writes plan files that TREK later executes or displays, unverified errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of ms-swift outputs before TREK uses them.
Mark ms-swift-generated content as untrusted in TREK.
Compare outputs against source data before publishing.
Limit ms-swift to drafting, not final decisions.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between generation and action.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles OIDC secrets, MFA secrets, email addresses, and reservation data, while ms-swift handles hub tokens and training/evaluation artifacts. The pair creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if TREK data is copied into ms-swift logs or checkpoints; the other agent is cited because the risk arises from cross-agent handling.
conditions: IF TREK personal data is copied into ms-swift logs, retention obligations may diverge.
IF ms-swift stores shared travel data in checkpoints or training outputs, deletion/export handling can break.
mitigations: Avoid placing personal travel data into ms-swift training artifacts.
Set short log retention on any shared workspace.
Delete shared files after each session.
Review whether any copied data includes email addresses or confirmation numbers.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
